note: [MS-XCA] 2.5 (the Windows NTFS compression format, RtlDecompressBuffer), written from the specification; no parameters, as in CyberChef. The chunk loop is a private primitive (an FL prototype cost 12 to 49 VM steps per output byte). Added: corrupt data is E_COERCE naming the fault (bad chunk signature, a chunk or word cut short, a match before the start of its chunk, a chunk that expands past 4096 bytes), and output past the value limit stops with E_LIMIT_VALUE. A zero header ends the data and bytes after it are ignored; empty input is empty output. Compression is not offered (CyberChef has none).

[MS-XCA] 2.3 and 2.4, Plain LZ77, written from the specification (the worked examples of section 3.1 are tests); no parameters. The decoder is a private primitive. Added: truncated data, a match before the start of the output and a bad long-length field are E_COERCE naming the fault, and output past the value limit stops with E_LIMIT_VALUE (a 32-bit match length allocates nothing). Empty input is E_COERCE because the stream starts with a flag word. Compression is not offered.

[MS-XCA] 2.1 and 2.2, LZ77+Huffman, written from the specification (the worked example of section 3.2 is a test); no parameters. The bit-level decoder is a private primitive. Blocks of 64 KiB follow one another, each with its own 256-byte table; the end-of-data symbol (256 with all input read) or a final 64 KiB block ends the data. Added: an over-subscribed or incomplete Huffman table, truncated data, a match before the start of the output and a bad long-length field are E_COERCE naming the fault, and output past the value limit stops with E_LIMIT_VALUE. Empty input is E_COERCE. Compression is not offered.
